note: Scam taxonomy for the synthetic message set (ARCHITECTURE.md 8.7). Fictional carrier 'Nimbus'. accountRisk: a recent message of this kind raises the risk on critical account actions (port-out PIN, SIM change), because these scams end with one.

categories.label: Fake carrier support
categories.description: Poses as Nimbus support or security and asks the customer to call back, confirm details, or follow instructions.
redFlags: asks you to call a number in the message
categories.advice: Nimbus never texts asking you to call a number or share details. Use the number on your bill or the Nimbus app.

categories.label: Code theft
categories.description: Asks the customer to send back a verification code they just received, usually framed as cancelling or confirming a request.
categories.advice: A code is only for you to type in yourself. Anyone asking you to read or send it is trying to get into your account.

categories.label: Transfer PIN request
categories.description: Asks for the number-transfer (port-out) PIN or to generate one, so the number can be moved to another carrier.
redFlags: asks for a transfer or port-out PIN
claims an upgrade or migration needs it
categories.advice: Your transfer PIN is only needed when you move your number yourself. Never read it to anyone.

categories.label: SIM deactivation threat
categories.description: Claims the SIM or line will be suspended unless the customer verifies at a link or installs a new eSIM profile.
redFlags: asks you to install an eSIM from a link
categories.advice: Nimbus does not suspend lines by text. Check your account in the Nimbus app or site, not through a link.

categories.label: Fake bill or payment problem
categories.description: Claims a payment failed or a bill is overdue and links to a page that collects card details.
categories.advice: Check your bill by signing in directly. Never enter card details from a text link.

categories.label: Fake reward or prize
categories.description: Offers loyalty points, a free phone, or a prize that needs a small shipping fee or login to claim.
categories.advice: Real rewards show up in your account. You never pay a fee to receive a prize.

categories.label: Fake delivery problem
categories.description: Says a package is held and asks for a redelivery or customs fee through a link.
categories.advice: Check deliveries in the shop's own app or site. Couriers do not text for redelivery fees.

categories.label: Fake toll, tax, or fine
categories.description: Claims an unpaid toll, tax, or fine with a penalty if not paid through a link.
categories.advice: Agencies send bills by mail or on their own site. Look up the agency yourself.

categories.label: Fake bank fraud alert
categories.description: Poses as a bank's fraud team about a suspicious charge and asks the customer to call or confirm details.
redFlags: asks for card or login details
categories.advice: Call the number on the back of your card, not one in a text.

categories.label: Family emergency or new number
categories.description: Poses as a relative on a new number who needs money urgently.
categories.advice: Call the person on the number you already have before sending anything.

categories.label: Wrong-number opener
categories.description: A friendly 'wrong number' message that starts a conversation leading to romance or investment fraud.
categories.advice: Don't reply to unknown 'wrong number' texts. Block and delete.

categories.label: Fake job or task offer
categories.description: Offers easy remote work, often 'rating products' for pay, that later demands deposits.
categories.advice: Real employers do not recruit by random text or ask you to pay to work.

categories.label: Investment or crypto scheme
categories.description: Promises guaranteed returns on crypto or trading through a group or app.
categories.advice: No real investment is guaranteed. Don't move money on advice from a text.

ham.label: Real carrier notice
ham.description: Bill ready, autopay done, plan change confirmed. No request for codes or PINs.

ham.label: Real verification code
ham.description: A code the customer asked for, with a warning not to share it.

ham.label: Real bank notice
ham.description: Balance or transaction notice that asks for nothing.

ham.label: Personal message
ham.description: Everyday text from someone the customer knows.

ham.label: Legitimate marketing
ham.description: A promotion from a known sender with opt-out.
